contentObjective: I can add and subtract decimals by lining up the place values and the decimal points.

vocabulary.definition: Combine or find the difference between decimals by lining up equal place values.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Combinar o hallar la diferencia entre decimales alineando valores posicionales iguales.
vocabulary.cloze: Line up equal ___ ___ before you add or subtract decimals.

examples.why: Equal place values sit in the same column.

examples.text: 12.4 + 3.75 with the last digits lined up
examples.why: Aligning the ends puts tenths under hundredths.

vocabulary.definition: A number with a dot, like 0.5, that shows a part less than one.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número con un punto, como 0.5, que muestra una parte menor que uno.
vocabulary.visual: 3.75 means 3 ones + 7 tenths + 5 hundredths — it is between 3 and 4
vocabulary.cloze: A number that uses a point to show a value less than one whole is a ___.

examples.why: A part less than one, written after the point.
Without the point it is five wholes.

vocabulary.definition: What a digit is worth based on where it sits in a number.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Lo que vale un dígito según el lugar que ocupa en el número.
vocabulary.visual: In 4.38: the 4 = 4 ones, the 3 = 3 tenths (0.3), the 8 = 8 hundredths (0.08)
vocabulary.cloze: The value a digit has based on its position in a number is its ___.

examples.why: Its worth comes from the column it sits in.
That reads the digit and ignores its column.

vocabulary.definition: The first spot after the decimal point. It shows parts out of 10.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El primer lugar después del punto decimal. Muestra partes de 10.
vocabulary.visual: 0.7 = 7/10 — like 7 slices of a pizza cut into 10 equal slices
vocabulary.cloze: The first place to the right of the decimal point is the ___ place.

examples.why: That 3 is in the hundredths place.

vocabulary.definition: The second spot after the decimal point. It shows parts out of 100.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El segundo lugar después del punto decimal. Muestra partes de 100.
vocabulary.visual: 0.05 = 5/100 — like 5 pennies out of a dollar (100 pennies)
vocabulary.cloze: The second place to the right of the decimal point is the ___ place.

examples.why: That 7 is in the tenths place.

vocabulary.definition: Adding zeros at the end of a decimal so numbers line up evenly.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Agregar ceros al final de un decimal para que los números se alineen.
vocabulary.visual: 15.7 becomes 15.70 so you can subtract 15.70 − 8.36 with aligned place values
vocabulary.cloze: Writing extra zeros at the end of a decimal so the places line up is called ___.

examples.why: The extra zero gives the hundredths column a digit.
That changes the value instead of padding it.

What a digit is worth based on where it sits

steps: 1. Line up the decimal points vertically by place value
2. Insert placeholder zeros so each number has the same number of decimal digits
3. Add or subtract right-to-left, regrouping as needed, and drop decimal straight down

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Cargo Bay Weight Log
revealWordProblem.text: The cargo bay scale reads 342.6 kilograms of supplies. The crew unloads 128.75 kilograms of food for the mess hall, and then loads 56.4 kilograms of water samples collected during the spacewalk. What is the final cargo weight on the scale? Explain your steps.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: First subtract the unloaded food: 342.60 − 128.75 = 213.85 kilograms. Then add the water samples, annexing a zero so 56.4 becomes 56.40: 213.85 + 56.40 = 270.25 kilograms. The final cargo weight is 270.25 kilograms.

questions.explanation: Line up decimals: 14.60 + 3.85. Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 6 + 8 = 14, write 4 carry 1. Ones: 4 + 3 + 1 = 8. Tens: 1. Answer: 18.45.
choiceFeedback: The tenths column here makes more than one whole ten tenths, and that regrouped 1 has to move into the ones column. Add the tenths first, carry, then finish the ones.
Recheck the tenths: 6 tenths + 8 tenths = 14 tenths. Write 4 in the tenths and carry 1 to the ones.
Look at the tenths again: 6 tenths plus 8 tenths. After you regroup a whole ten tenths out of that total, check carefully how many tenths are really left over.
hints: Notice the mismatch: 14.6 has one decimal place but 3.85 has two. Lining up the POINTS is the whole trick here.
Write 14.6 as 14.60 so both numbers show hundredths, stack the decimal points, and add column by column from the right.
Set up 14.60 + 3.85 with the points stacked. Add the hundredths (0 + 5) first, then the tenths (6 + 8) — that column carries.
questions.explanationEs: Alinea los decimales: 14.60 + 3.85. Centésimas: 0 + 5 = 5. Décimas: 6 + 8 = 14, escribe 4 y lleva 1. Unidades: 4 + 3 + 1 = 8. Decenas: 1. Respuesta: 18.45.
hintsEs: Fíjate en la diferencia: 14.6 tiene un decimal pero 3.85 tiene dos. Alinear los PUNTOS es todo el truco aquí.
Escribe 14.6 como 14.60 para que ambos muestren centésimas, alinea los puntos decimales y suma columna por columna desde la derecha.
Acomoda 14.60 + 3.85 con los puntos alineados. Suma primero las centésimas (0 + 5) y luego las décimas (6 + 8): esa columna lleva.

questions.explanation: Rewrite as 20.30 − 7.48. Annex a zero so both have two decimal places. Work carefully with borrowing: 20.30 − 7.48 = 12.82.
choiceFeedback: Check it: 12.18 + 7.48 = 19.66, not 20.3. Rewrite 20.3 as 20.30, line up the points, and regroup in each column.
You borrowed for the hundredths, but the tenths digit on top has to shrink by one when you do that. Redo the tenths column using the smaller digit.
13.82 is one whole too many. Borrowing for the tenths takes 1 from the ones, so 20 becomes 19 before you subtract 7.
hints: 20.3 stops at the tenths but 7.48 has hundredths — you can't subtract from an empty column until you annex a zero.
Rewrite the problem as 20.30 − 7.48, stack the decimal points, and subtract right to left, borrowing when the top digit is smaller.
Start at the hundredths: 0 − 8 doesn't work, so borrow from the tenths to make it 10 − 8. Keep borrowing leftward as needed.
questions.explanationEs: Reescribe como 20.30 − 7.48. Agrega un cero para que ambos números tengan dos cifras decimales. Trabaja con cuidado al pedir prestado: 20.30 − 7.48 = 12.82.
hintsEs: 20.3 llega solo a las décimas pero 7.48 tiene centésimas: no puedes restar de una columna vacía sin agregar un cero.
Reescribe el problema como 20.30 − 7.48, alinea los puntos decimales y resta de derecha a izquierda, pidiendo prestado cuando el dígito de arriba sea menor.
Empieza en las centésimas: 0 − 8 no se puede, así que pide prestado a las décimas para que sea 10 − 8. Sigue pidiendo prestado hacia la izquierda.

questions.explanation: Line up decimals: 9.05 + 4.70. Hundredths: 5 + 0 = 5. Tenths: 0 + 7 = 7. Ones: 9 + 4 = 13. Answer: 13.75.
choiceFeedback: Line up the decimal points—are the place values matched?
The tenths and hundredths digits are switched. Write 4.7 as 4.70 so tenths sit under tenths and hundredths under hundredths before you add.
An extra whole slipped into your answer. Nothing regroups out of the tenths in this problem, so add only 9 + 4 in the ones column.
hints: Watch the middle zero in 9.05 and the missing hundredths in 4.7 — align the decimal POINTS, never the last digits.
Write 4.7 as 4.70, stack the two numbers with the points lined up, then add each column starting from the right.
Stack 9.05 over 4.70. Add hundredths (5 + 0), then tenths (0 + 7), then the ones — watch that last sum spill into a tens place.
questions.explanationEs: Alinea los decimales: 9.05 + 4.70. Centésimas: 5 + 0 = 5. Décimas: 0 + 7 = 7. Unidades: 9 + 4 = 13. Respuesta: 13.75.
hintsEs: Observa el cero de en medio en 9.05 y las centésimas que faltan en 4.7: alinea los PUNTOS decimales, nunca el último dígito.
Escribe 4.7 como 4.70, acomoda los dos números con los puntos alineados y suma cada columna empezando por la derecha.
Acomoda 9.05 sobre 4.70. Suma centésimas (5 + 0), luego décimas (0 + 7) y luego las unidades; fíjate que esa suma pasa a las decenas.

steps: 1. Line up the decimal points vertically by place value
2. Insert placeholder zeros so each number has the same number of decimal digits
3. Add or subtract right-to-left, regrouping as needed, and drop decimal straight down
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Add and Subtract Decimals is lining up the last digits (the right edges) of each number instead of lining up the decimal points — for example, adding 8.3 and 2.45 as if the 3 and the 5 belong in the same column. Before you add or subtract, add zeros so every number has the same number of decimal places (write 8.3 as 8.30), then check that the decimal points sit directly above one another.

level2.stemEs: Eva suma 3.4 + 1.25. Alinea los últimos dígitos y obtiene 1.59. ¿Cuál es la suma correcta?
hints: Line up the decimal points, not the last digits. Write 3.4 as 3.40.
hintsEs: Alinea los puntos decimales, no los últimos dígitos. Escribe 3.4 como 3.40.

level2.stem: A pencil costs $0.65. A pen costs $1.40. How much more does the pen cost?

hintsEs: Resta el costo menor del costo mayor. Alinea los puntos decimales.
level2.explanation: Line up the decimal points: 1.40 − 0.65 Subtract from right to left. Regroup: 1.40 − 0.65 = 0.75
level2.explanationEs: Alinea los puntos decimales: 1.40 − 0.65 Resta de derecha a izquierda. Reagrupa: 1.40 − 0.65 = 0.75

hints: Write 6 as 6.00. Then subtract every column, starting with the hundredths.

level3.stem: A scale reads 3.2 kg. A box that weighs 1.875 kg is taken off. What does the scale read now?

hints: 1.875 has thousandths. Write 3.2 as 3.200 so the places match.
hintsEs: 1.875 tiene milésimos. Escribe 3.2 como 3.200 para que los lugares coincidan.
